problem_sources.text: ﻿HACK IN HILLS ’26 Problem Statements & Challenge Tracks 01. Vision-Based Autonomous Robot Problem Statement Build an autonomous robot that uses an AI-powered vision system to understand its surroundings, identify relevant objects and people, and navigate autonomously toward a given objective while detecting and avoiding obstacles. Suggested Technical Directions * Object detection * Image classification * Scene understanding * Vision-language models * Motor control * Sensors and perception * Autonomous navigation * Obstacle detection and avoidance * Real-time decision making Challenge Create a functional robotic prototype demonstrating how AI vision can be combined with robotics for autonomous perception, navigation, and decision-making in the physical world. Teams may demonstrate the system in a real or simulated environment. 02. Onchain Finance & Trading Problem Statement Build a fully onchain financial product that leverages fast blockchain settlement to create innovative and transparent trading or lending markets without relying on centralized offchain infrastructure. Possible Directions * Fully onchain order books with matching and settlement handled onchain. * Perpetual futures markets with funding rates updated every block. * Undercollateralized lending using a user’s onchain credit history to determine lending terms. * Onchain market-making systems that provide liquidity and dynamically respond to market conditions. Challenge Create a functional prototype demonstrating how blockchain-native infrastructure can enable financial products that are difficult, inefficient, or less transparent to build using traditional centralized systems. Clearly demonstrate the onchain components, transaction flow, and core financial mechanism. 03. Commodity Derivatives Intelligence Problem Statement Build a data product using India’s public commodity futures data to identify and analyze relative pricing differences between contracts representing the same underlying metal. MCX lists gold futures in multiple contract sizes, including GOLDM, GOLDTEN, GOLDGUINEA, and GOLDPETAL. Because these contracts represent the same underlying metal, their normalized prices should be closely related. The challenge is to understand, measure, and responsibly analyze the differences between them. Possible Directions Cross-Contract Relative Value * Normalize contract size, quotation base, and purity. * Identify when one contract appears unusually cheap or expensive relative to another. Term Structure & Carry Analytics * Analyze the futures curve. * Separate mechanical roll-down toward expiry from genuine changes in the curve. Walk-Forward Backtesting * Replay historical contracts day by day without look-ahead bias. * Account for transaction costs and thin-day liquidity. Trader-Facing Intelligence * Build dashboards or alerts that highlight meaningful opportunities. * Keep alerts quiet when there is no meaningful signal. * Attribute performance to the strategy rather than simply to gold-price movement. Contract Lifecycle Planning * Track listing dates, liquidity development, tender periods, and expiry. * Place every intended entry and exit inside the relevant contract calendar. Data Sources MCX Daily Bhavcopy: https://www.mcxindia.com/market-data/bhavcopy MCX Gold Contract Specifications: https://www.mcxindia.com/products/bullion/gold The daily Bhavcopy provides Symbol, Date, ExpiryDate, Open, High, Low, Close, Volume, and OpenInterest. The data is publicly available and does not require an API key. Important Data Considerations * Validate the returned Date against the requested date. MCX may return the most recent available trading day for an unrecognized, holiday, malformed, or future date. * Requests use DD/MM/YYYY, while the response Date uses MM/DD/YYYY. ExpiryDate uses a compact format such as 04SEP2026, and Symbol values may be space-padded. * Track contracts by expiry_date rather than using a continuous near-month series. A near-month series changes contracts at expiry and can create artificial price jumps. * Settlement prices are official exchange settlement values and should not automatically be treated as executable fill prices, particularly for thin contracts. * Volume is not the same as market depth or available liquidity. * GOLDTEN is available only from its 2025 listing period onward; comparisons involving GOLDTEN therefore have a shorter history. Contract Mechanics Contract Trading Unit Price Quoted Per Purity Expiry Window GOLDM 100 g 10 g 995 3rd–5th GOLDTEN 10 g 10 g 999 27th–31st GOLDGUINEA 8 g 8 g 999 27th–31st GOLDPETAL 1 g 1 g 999 27th–31st Challenge Create a functional prototype that transforms exchange settlement data into a defensible analytical signal or intelligence product and validates the approach using unseen historical data. Where a strategy or signal is presented, report performance after relevant costs using the prices of the contracts actually held, and clearly separate strategy performance from the impact of the underlying gold price. A rigorous demonstration that no persistent edge survives costs is also a valid analytical outcome. The objective is analytical rigor rather than generating a signal every day. 04. Securing Adversarial AI Safety Testing Infrastructure — Bayora Introduction AI systems are increasingly being deployed in areas where reliability, security, and safety are critical. As these systems become more capable, robust adversarial testing and safety validation infrastructure is essential. Bayora is an AI safety validation platform built around a red-team / blue-team model. The red team systematically tests language models using adversarial prompts, jailbreak sequences, and injection strategies, while the blue team develops defensive countermeasures. Together, they form a continuous adversarial testing loop intended to identify safety failures before deployment. HACK IN HILLS ’26 | MANALI ️

Not a Marathon. A Mountain Sprint.

Hosted by Builder Base × Nexido × Web3 India

UPDATE: REGISTRATIONS EXTENDED + TINYFISH BUILDER CHALLENGE INTRODUCED

More time to build. A new challenge to explore.

Hack in Hills ’26 registrations and Idea & PPT submissions have been extended by 5 days, until 15 October 2026, 11:59 PM IST.

We're also introducing the TinyFish Builder Challenge, an opportunity for builders to explore AI agents, live-web automation and real-world applications using TinyFish.

TinyFish Builder Challenge Form: https://forms.gle/TCW5jukdGB6bnRm19

About Hack in Hills ’26

Hack in Hills ’26 is a 24+ hour offline hackathon in Manali, bringing together developers, designers, AI builders, Web3 developers, creators and innovators to build solutions to real-world problems.

The journey starts online with ideas, moves into prototype development and public pitching, and concludes with the Grand Finale in the Himalayas.

What to Expect

  • Free registration

  • Team size: 1–3 members

  • Top 500 teams shortlisted after Round 1

  • Top 40 finalist builders invited to Manali

  • 24+ hours of offline building

  • Mentors, speakers, judges and ecosystem networking

  • ₹50,000 cash bounty pool

  • AI, Web3, software development and emerging technology

  • TinyFish Builder Challenge

  • Grand Finale: 20–21 November 2026, Manali

NEW: TinyFish Builder Challenge

What if your AI could go beyond answering questions and actually get work done on the web?

The TinyFish Builder Challenge invites participants to explore web-connected AI agents and build useful automations, research tools and applications using TinyFish.

Participants can explore TinyFish independently or use it within their Hack in Hills projects.

How to Participate

Step 1: Get Started with TinyFish

Visit https://tinyfish.hackinhills.com and create your TinyFish account.

New accounts can access $8 in starting TinyFish credits, subject to TinyFish's terms and eligibility.

Step 2: Connect and Run TinyFish

Connect TinyFish with a supported AI assistant or development environment, such as ChatGPT or Claude, and complete your first successful TinyFish run.

Step 3: Complete the Community Tasks

Follow TinyFish on X: https://x.com/Tiny_Fish

Follow Hack in Hills on X: https://x.com/HackInHills

Share your TinyFish onboarding or builder experience on X using the campaign instructions provided in the form.

Step 4: Submit the Challenge Form

Complete the required onboarding and social tasks and submit your details and requested proof.

Official Form: https://forms.gle/TCW5jukdGB6bnRm19

Build With TinyFish

Builders are encouraged to explore practical applications such as:

  • AI agents that interact with websites

  • Automated research and information gathering

  • Intelligent browsing and workflow automation

  • Web-connected assistants

  • AI-powered productivity and developer tools

  • Real-world automation applications

The TinyFish Builder Challenge is an additional opportunity. Participation is optional and does not replace the main Hack in Hills Unstop registration or project-submission requirements.

Hackathon Stages & Timeline

Round 1: Idea & PPT Submission

10 September – 15 October 2026

Mode: Online

Submit your hackathon idea using the official PPT template.

Your submission should cover:

  • Problem Statement

  • Proposed Solution

  • Innovation & Uniqueness

  • Target Users & Use Case

  • Technical Architecture / Tech Stack

  • Expected Impact

  • Implementation Roadmap

Participants interested in TinyFish may also describe how they plan to use AI agents or web automation in their solution.

Deadline: 15 October 2026, 11:59 PM IST

The Top 500 teams will advance to Round 2.

Round 1 Shortlisting

16–17 October 2026

Submitted ideas will be evaluated on relevance, innovation, feasibility, expected impact and implementation approach.

Shortlisted teams will receive instructions for the next stage.

Round 2A: Prototype Development

18–24 October 2026

Mode: Online

The Top 500 shortlisted teams will develop a functional prototype based on their selected problem statement.

Teams should:

  • Build a functional prototype or MVP

  • Demonstrate the core solution

  • Maintain a GitHub repository

  • Show technical feasibility and usability

  • Prepare a short demo video

Teams participating in the TinyFish Builder Challenge are encouraged to demonstrate a functional TinyFish-powered use case where relevant.

Round 2B: Social Pitch & Outreach

24–27 October 2026

Mode: Online

Shortlisted teams must complete the following:

1. LinkedIn Pitch

Publish a LinkedIn post presenting your project idea, proposed solution, and what makes it unique.

Tag Eren, Builder Base, Nexido and Web3 India.

2. Instagram Reel

Create a short Instagram Reel explaining why your team wants to participate in Hack in Hills ’26, what you are building and what makes your project interesting.

Tag Eren.dev, Builder Base, Nexido and Web3 India.

3. Prototype Demo + GitHub

Submit a short demo video showcasing your working prototype and your GitHub repository link.

All required submission links must be provided through the designated Round 2 submission form.

Final submission deadline: 27 October 2026, 11:59 PM IST

Final Evaluation & Finalists Announcement

Evaluation: 28–29 October 2026

Projects will be assessed on innovation, problem-solution fit, functional implementation, technical execution, impact, usability and presentation.

Finalists Announced: 30 October 2026

The Top 40 builders will be selected for the Grand Finale in Manali.

Round 3: Grand Finale

20–21 November 2026

Location: Manali, Himachal Pradesh

Format: 24+ Hours | Offline

Finalist teams will build, refine and present their projects in front of mentors and judges while competing for the ₹50,000 cash bounty pool.

Problem Statements

Explore the official Hack in Hills ’26 Problem Statements:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1L9XKOlZ2y7Icbgwl7zhjNb-v8NOng8eddmJ1hfDTpb8/edit

Teams should carefully review the available tracks and problem requirements before preparing submissions.

Important Links

Official Website: https://hackinhills.com

TinyFish Onboarding: https://tinyfish.hackinhills.com

TinyFish Builder Challenge Form: https://forms.gle/TCW5jukdGB6bnRm19

HIH Participants WhatsApp Group: https://chat.whatsapp.com/H1T0MGDhYV9CRyNWBagSAz

Ready to Build?

Five extra days. One more reason to start building.

Take your idea from PPT → Prototype → Pitch → Mountain Finale.

Not a Marathon. A Mountain Sprint. ️
